title: Anticipating or Speculating? Making Futures Pay in AI Ethics
abstract: arXiv:2611.22268v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Philosophers have recently been trying to develop uniform decision rules for instances in which physicians' judgments diverge from the recommendations of medical artificial intelligence (AI) systems. I argue that this effort is fatally flawed because the performance and appropriate use of algorithmic recommendation systems by physicians are highly context-specific, empirical medical matters rather than epistemological ones. In such instances, general decision rules can be stipulated only to the extent that they abstract away from relevant, indeed determinative, contextual circumstances. The alleged problem of physician-AI disagreement, and others like it, play into longstanding disputes in technology ethics about the viability and utility of envisioning possible futures: is this useful "anticipation" or wasteful "speculation"? translated_title: 预见还是投机？让未来思考在AI伦理中真正产生价值
translated_abstract: 哲学家们近来一直试图为医生的判断与医疗人工智能（AI）系统的建议出现分歧的情形制定统一的决策规则。我认为这一努力存在致命缺陷，因为医生对算法推荐系统的表现评估和恰当使用是高度依赖具体情境的、经验性的医学问题，而非认识论问题。在这类情形中，一般性决策规则只有通过抽象掉相关的——实际上是具有决定性的——情境因素才能被规定。所谓的医生-AI分歧问题以及其他类似问题，实际上牵涉到技术伦理中关于构想可能未来的可行性与实用性的长期争论：这究竟是有用的“预见”还是无益的“投机”？我认为二者是可以加以区分的。预见通过探索合理的未来图景来帮助指导当前的行动……
tldr: 本文论证了为医生与医疗AI分歧制定统一决策规则的努力存在根本缺陷，因为算法推荐的恰当使用是高度情境化的经验性医学问题，并提出应区分技术伦理中有价值的“预见”与无益的“投机”。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that efforts to establish uniform decision rules for physician-AI disagreement are fatally flawed, since the appropriate use of algorithmic recommendations is a highly context-specific empirical medical matter, and it proposes distinguishing useful "anticipation" from wasteful "speculation" in technology ethics.
